headline: Evidence Gap, Strategy Gap
thesis: Vendors claim AI works and provosts use it daily, but few can show independent evidence or a campus-wide strategy behind it.
summary: EdReports found that only one of 10 edtech providers cited third-party evidence of student outcomes for its AI features, even as nearly all call them effective. In higher ed, Inside Higher Ed's provost survey shows about 7 in 10 provosts use AI weekly but only 1 in 10 report a centralized institutional AI strategy. Meanwhile early-childhood educators are pushing back on AI-generated video, Brookings keeps framing AI as helpful only when narrowly and carefully designed, and EdTech Week (NYC) and UPCEA Convergence arrive next week.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 9, 2026 · Direct site fetches were unavailable, so items come from search-indexed results; most sources had no new dated news today and list recent or evergreen items. EdTech Week dates vary by listing (Oct 12–16 vs. Oct 14–15).
